dedupe_keys.name: united states resilience of food energy and water systems to the covid 19 labour shortage

description: This case study measures how a sudden labour shortage affects the systems that produce, distribute and deliver food, energy and water, treating them as one interdependent system. The authors, at Sam Houston State University and Merrimack College, developed resilience metrics based on unserved demand, calculated the labour intensity of production in each system, and applied them to the labour shortage in the United States caused by the COVID-19 pandemic; the work is published in a journal article that is free to read online as a PDF on the publisher's site. Coverage is national. Caveats: the analysis relies on aggregate labour intensity and demand data, and the adjustments tested are stylised. The study found that a labour shortage can significantly reduce the performance of the combined system, possibly because food and water systems depend heavily on energy and energy is costly to store, and that the food system was more resilient than the energy and water systems because many food alternatives can meet demand in each food category. Simulation uses: labour disruption scenarios and resilience metrics for interdependent food, energy and water models. Related records: the study of catastrophic electricity loss and food supply (case_study-catastrophic-electricity-loss-food-supply-system-dynamics) models the energy dependency of food supply in more detail.
